chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man asked me about a woman who died and had not performed Hajj, and she bequeathed [money] to be used for Hajj. I was asked about it: if it was more preferable that it be placed among the poor of the offspring of Fatimah, it was placed among them; and if Hajj was more preferable, Hajj was performed for her. So I said to him: If an obligatory Hajj was due upon her, then spending what she bequeathed on Hajj is more beloved to me than distributing it in other than that.
ai.seo_question: What is the preferred use of a bequest for Hajj if the deceased woman owed an obligatory Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia juristic principle of 'al-ashlah' (choosing the more beneficial option) when executing a bequest for Hajj. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the obligatory Hajj, which takes precedence, and the discretionary use of funds, allowing for distribution to the 'poor of the children of Fatima' if that yields greater spiritual or social benefit. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on the Ahl al-Bayt's lineage as a primary recipient of charity and the flexibility in fulfilling religious duties based on contextual wisdom.
